story: Vyasa, son of the sage Parashara and the fisherwoman Satyavati, divided the one Veda into four and composed the Mahabharata, dictating it to Ganesha. He was also the father of Dhritarashtra, Pandu and Vidura, which makes him the grandfather of both the Kauravas and the Pandavas.
belief: He is honoured as one of the greatest sages and as an immortal. Guru Purnima, the festival of teachers, is also called Vyasa Purnima.
turns: He knew how the story would end and did not stop the war his grandsons fought. Some see that as wisdom; others see it as standing by.
facts: His full name is Krishna Dvaipayana, 'the dark one born on an island'.
Tradition also credits him with the 18 Puranas.
The Mahabharata has about 100,000 verses, the longest epic poem ever composed.
